builder_plan.scenario: A self-hosted assistant is too expensive because its model uses most of the GPU memory.
builder_plan.change: Try the paper's supported lower-precision weights on a copy of your serving setup.
builder_plan.baseline: The same model at its original precision, on the same GPU.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Peak memory, task pass rate, latency, and total serving cost at the same context and load.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: What Does 4-Bit Microscaling Cost a Wearable Activity Recognizer?
summary: The technique replaces full-precision (FP32/FP16) or 8-bit integer quantization of weights and activations with 4-bit block-scaled floating-point formats (MXFP4, NVFP4) to cut model storage and memory traffic on-device. Costs: simulated 4-bit weights-plus-activations quantization degrades accuracy (0.75 F1 points with NVFP4, 5.14 with MXFP4), and MXFP4's reference scale-rounding-down rule clips block maxima unless corrected to round-up plus an 8-bit FP scale. What can fail: results are simulated rather than measured on real 4-bit hardware for a single small 1D CNN on one dataset, MXFP4 degrades sharply under naive scale selection, and gains may not transfer to other models, tasks, or actual silicon.
rationale: The reader runs constrained single-GPU or API infrastructure rather than wearable 4-bit hardware, so the NVFP4-over-MXFP4 finding is useful guidance for future edge quantization but requires hardware- and workload-specific validation before adoption.
technique: 4-bit microscaling formats (MXFP4, NVFP4) for wearable HAR

claims.statement: The technique replaces full-precision (FP32/FP16) or 8-bit integer quantization of weights and activations with 4-bit block-scaled floating-point formats (MXFP4, NVFP4) to cut model storage and memory traffic on-device. Costs: simulated 4-bit weights-plus-activations quantization degrades accuracy (0.75 F1 points with NVFP4, 5.14 with MXFP4), and MXFP4's reference scale-rounding-down rule clips block maxima unless corrected to round-up plus an 8-bit FP scale. What can fail: results are simulated rather than measured on real 4-bit hardware for a single small 1D CNN on one dataset, MXFP4 degrades sharply under naive scale selection, and gains may not transfer to other models, tasks, or actual silicon.

With 4-bit weights and activations, NVFP4 loses only 0.75 macro-F1 points versus 5.14 for MXFP4 on a 159k-parameter wearable CNN, and wins all five held-out-player folds; FP16/INT8 lose at most 0.16 points.
